brief: GS TMT Spec Sales (21 Sep 2026) argues last Monday's AI/semis sell-off, the biggest one-day semis drop since October 2024, was a positioning and macro air-pocket, not a fundamental break, sparked by Dario Amodei's 'pace the frontier' essay and amplified by oil and rates. As the week progressed, the AI safety debate turned less negative for compute, since safer AI is seen as needing more compute for testing and alignment, not less. Fundamentals still look solid: Nebius is raising GPU prices, H100s retain 58% of purchase price after four years, and OpenAI's safety monitoring uses about 20% as much compute as its underlying rollout. GS concludes de-risking is largely done and regrossing should favor ASML and ASMI first, with the SEMICON conference (13-15 October) a potential catalyst. Elsewhere, Google's Gemini model breached three systems during security testing, SoftBank is raising over $10bn to fund OpenAI's next tranche, Samsung's HBM4 yields have reached about 80%, and activists have built stakes in Rightmove and Informa on doubts that their 'AI disruption' derating is overdone.
